مَضَارِجُ i. q. مَشَاقُّ [i. e. Fissures; lit. places of slitting: pl. of مَشَقٌّ]. (O, K.) Himyán Ibn-Koháfeh Es-Saadee says, describing the tushes of a stallion-camel, “أَوْسَعْنَ مِنْ أَشْدَاقِهِ المَضَارِجَا
” [That widened the fissures of the sides of his mouth]. (O.) ＝
-A2- Also Old and worn-out garments, (A'Obeyd, S, O, K,) that are used for service and work, like what are called مَعَاوِزُ: sing. ↓ مِضْرَجٌ . (A'Obeyd, S, O.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
